title: The standard t-structure on the integral category
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a noetherian scheme of finite dimension on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $P_n=A/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$, the completed coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and write
$$
 D=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)),\qquad \mathcal C=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)\subset D
$$
for the full bounded constructible complete category, including compatible etale-origin witnesses, of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Let $\mathcal H^i$ denote the ambient cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Set
$$
 \mathcal C^{\leq0}=\{K\in\mathcal C:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\text{ for all }i>0\},\qquad
 \mathcal C^{\geq0}=\{K\in\mathcal C:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\text{ for all }i<0\}.
$$
With the inherited shift and distinguished triangles, these form a bounded t-structure [def-weil-t-structure] on $\mathcal C$. Its truncation functors are the restrictions of the canonical ambient truncations $\tau_D^{\leq m}$ and $\tau_D^{\geq m}$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$, with their canonical maps and triangles; its heart consists exactly of the objects whose ambient cohomology sheaves vanish in every degree other than zero.

For any $K\in\mathcal C$ satisfying the Tor-compatibility hypothesis of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] at every level of its normalized reduction tower $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, these same canonical truncations are the derived limits of the levelwise truncated towers specified in that theorem, with its canonical reduction isomorphisms and normalization compatibility. The general t-structure assertion does not impose this additional hypothesis on every object.

An object is called $\varpi$-power-torsion here if $\varpi^N\operatorname{id}_K=0$ in $\mathcal C$ for some integer $N\geq1$, using the scalar endomorphisms induced by multiplication on complexes of $A_T$-modules. Both truncation functors preserve this condition with the same exponent: for every such $K,N$ and every $m\in\mathbf Z$,
$$
 \varpi^N\operatorname{id}_{\tau^{\leq m}K}=0,\qquad
 \varpi^N\operatorname{id}_{\tau^{\geq m}K}=0.
$$

proof.text: Apply pbcIntegralUniformComplete_isTriangulated to the finite coefficient extension, T, and the given finite-dimensional and stalkwise invertibility hypotheses. Its second component is exactly the ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated instance required for the published full subcategory. The inherited structure and exact full inclusion are those of Mathlib triangulated subcategories.

Apply Mathlib ObjectProperty.HasInducedTStructure.mk' to pbcIntegralCanonicalTruncations_mem, with the ambient object and membership proof bundled as an object of the full subcategory. This gives the induced t-structure without a Tor hypothesis. The constructor uses the canonical ambient truncation triangle; its degree conditions and orthogonality are the standard ambient t-structure axioms.

Stalkwise invertibility of the coefficient prime implies invertibility of its global section by RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ. Apply the two implications of integralStratifiedPerfectCharacterization to the membership proof of K. Its bounded-cohomology condition supplies integers a,b and ambient IsGE a and IsLE b. ObjectProperty.tStructure_isGE_iff and tStructure_isLE_iff transfer these witnesses to the induced category, proving bounded = top. For the heart, use mem_heart_iff and the same two induced-membership equivalences. DerivedCategory.isLE_iff and isGE_iff identify the two conditions with vanishing in positive and negative degrees. Splitting a nonzero integer into the negative and positive cases proves exactly the stated heart characterization.

The full inclusion is t-exact: in every degree its preservation of the two halves is exactly ObjectProperty.tStructure_isLE_iff and tStructure_isGE_iff. It commutes with shifts and is triangulated by the inherited structure. Apply the existing, proved upstream Functor.eTruncLTIso at m+1 and Functor.eTruncGEIso at m in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.SpectralObject. Integer extended truncations are definitionally the required truncLE and truncGE. These natural isomorphisms are characterized by the canonical counit and unit, as in the uniqueness/adjunction assertion. The conditional tower computation remains the separately published pbc_integral_truncations theorem, through the retained public import; no additional Tor hypothesis enters the induced structure.

For shift linearity, transport linearity of inclusion followed by ambient shift across the inverse inclusion/shift comparison. Faithfulness of the inclusion then reflects the scalar equation, giving linearity of the inherited shift. For torsion, set r to the Nth power of the uniformizer and assume r times id_K is zero. Postcompose the lower truncation scalar identity with the canonical counit, and precompose the upper scalar identity with the canonical unit. Bilinearity identifies both composites with the corresponding composites with r times id_K, hence with zero. Apply the proved adjunction injectivity lemmas to_truncLE_obj_ext and from_truncGE_obj_ext. The source and target bounds hold by the truncation instances. Both truncated identities are therefore killed by the original exponent, without requiring linearity of a truncation functor as an additional assumption.

lean.statement: theorem pbc_integral_tstructure : (pbcIntegralTStructure T l E).bounded = ⊤ ∧ (∀ K : PbcBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcIntegralDatum l E), (pbcIntegralTStructure T l E).heart K ↔ ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K.obj)) ∧ (∀ m : ℤ, Nonempty ((pbcIntegralTStructure T l E).truncLE m ⋙ (ObjectProperty.ι (PbcIsBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcIntegralDatum l E))) ≅ (ObjectProperty.ι (PbcIsBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcIntegralDatum l E))) ⋙ (pbcAmbientTStructure T l E).truncLE m) ∧ Nonempty ((pbcIntegralTStructure T l E).truncGE m ⋙ (ObjectProperty.ι (PbcIsBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcIntegralDatum l E))) ≅ (ObjectProperty.ι (PbcIsBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcIntegralDatum l E))) ⋙ (pbcAmbientTStructure T l E).truncGE m)) ∧ ∀ (K : PbcBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcIntegralDatum l E)) (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → (pbcUniformizer l E) ^ N • 𝟙 K = 0 → ∀ m : ℤ, (pbcUniformizer l E) ^ N • 𝟙 (((pbcIntegralTStructure T l E).truncLE m).obj K) = 0 ∧ (pbcUniformizer l E) ^ N • 𝟙 (((pbcIntegralTStructure T l E).truncGE m).obj K) = 0

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations], set
$$
 (\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A))^{\le0}:=\{K:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\ \forall i>0\},
$$
$$
 (\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A))^{\ge0}:=\{K:\mathcal H^i(K)=0\ \forall i<0\}.
$$
These form a bounded t-structure on $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, whose truncation
functors are the $\tau^{\le m},\tau^{\ge m}$ of
[thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] and whose heart consists of the objects
with cohomology concentrated in degree zero. The subcategory of
$\varpi$-power-torsion objects is stable under the truncation functors.

proof.text:
The shift conditions and the orthogonality of a t-structure, namely
$\Hom(A,B[-1])=0$ for $A\in(\Dbc)^{\le0}$, $B\in(\Dbc)^{\ge0}$, are the
corresponding ambient statements for the standard t-structure of
$D(T_{\Proet},A)$, since $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ is a full subcategory and its
objects' cohomology sheaves are the ambient ones. The truncation axiom and
the truncation triangles are [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations] (ii)--(iii)
with the cohomology formulas of (ii) showing the end terms to lie in the
claimed subcategories. Boundedness: by the reconstruction lemma for uniform
towers (and its use in [thm-weil-pbc-integral-truncations]), an object's
local models are supported in a finite interval $[d_0,d_1]$, so its
cohomology vanishes outside it; the interval is part of the data of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Finally the truncation
functors are additive and $A_T$-linear, so if $\varpi^n\cdot1_K=0$ in
$\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$, then
$\varpi^n\cdot1_{\tau^{\le m}K}=\tau^{\le m}(\varpi^n\cdot1_K)=0$, and
similarly for $\tau^{\ge m+1}$.
